newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Indian GDRs ease before market holiday.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Indian GDRs ease before market holiday.

text.p: Indian GDRs eased for a second day running after their recent post-budget rally and traders said the lull was likely to continue until early next week.
Indian stock exchanges will be closed on Friday for the Mahashivratri holiday, which means London GDR trading will get no support from Bombay moving into the weekend.
"We're seeing profit-taking after the recent rises ahead of the market holiday," said one dealer. "GDR buying is not aggressive, we're seeing stale bulls that are not going anywhere."
Another trader said the weakness would persist for another couple of sessions as players waited for more attractive levels.

The market is starting to gear up for the launch of a jumbo issue of GDRs for overseas telecommunications monopoly VSNL. Roadshows are set to begin in Hong Kong on March 10, with pricing and allocation set for March 24.
Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, Jardine Fleming and Salomon Brothers are acting as joint global coordinators and bookrunners.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed down 0.89 points, or 1.15 percent, at 76.46 points, with the premium over the local market at 15.53 percent compared with Wednesday's 14.84 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index ended near the day's lows, down 1.65 percent at 3,870.26, with end-of-account trading depressing prices.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended up 0.93 percent, or 0.55 points, at 59.09 points, a premium of 39.28 percent over the local market.
The Korea Composite Index rose 3.21 points to 678.11 in brisk trading boosted by hints of changes to its real-name financial regulations.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 1.98 percent, or 2.09 points, at 107.70, a premium of 0.77 percent.
The Taiwan Weighted Index closed at another six-year high, up 0.77 percent at 8,081, with market sentiment strong despite central bank comments about its worries over the market's sizzling rally.
